entities.summary: Pierre de Foix, le vieux, was a French cardinal created in 1409 and played a significant role in the governance of the Catholic Church during the Late Middle Ages. He served as the Archbishop of Toulouse and the Bishop of Valence, and his leadership during the Council of Pontoise in 1419 helped to resolve a major dispute within the Church. His legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, as he contributed to the development of the University of Toulouse and the establishment of the Order of the Golden Fleece. Pierre de Foix, le vieux, died on December 22, 1464, and his remains were interred in the cathedral of Toulouse. The city of Toulouse still honors his memory through the Place Pierre-de-Foix, a vibrant square in the heart of the city. Pierre de Foix, le vieux, was a key figure in the French Renaissance, known for his intelligence, wisdom, and spiritual guidance. He played a crucial role in the development of the Catholic Church's doctrine and practices, and his influence can still be felt in the modern-day religious landscape. Pierre de Foix, le vieux, was also a patron of the arts, and his love of literature and music helped to foster a thriving cultural scene in Toulouse. He was a true Renaissance man, and his legacy continues to inspire and educate people to this day.
